- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s reversal potential.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing or lagged decay to prevent immediate overcorrection.
- If last 3–5 days show mean reversion (price moving back toward prior range), model often fails to recognize it; increase downward bias or add mean-reversion term.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 14-day average to avoid horizon drift.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.6 → +0.6), model often misreads momentum; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen false momentum signals.
